title: Feature Importance & Explainability
interviewAnswer: Feature importance can mean different things: model-specific impurity scores, permutation importance, SHAP-style local/global explanations, or coefficients. Interpret with care when features are correlated.
why: Explainability questions test whether you know what a model used, what caused an outcome, and what an explanation method can legitimately claim.
intuition: Feature importance asks how much predictions depend on a feature, but different methods answer different versions of that question. No importance score automatically proves causality.
deepDive: Linear coefficients are model-specific and depend on scale and collinearity. Tree impurity importance can favor high-cardinality or frequently split features. Permutation importance measures performance degradation after breaking a feature association but becomes ambiguous with correlated features. SHAP-style methods allocate prediction differences according to a game-theoretic framework, but their interpretation depends on background and feature-dependence assumptions.
workedExample: If two features are near-duplicates, permutation of one may show little importance because the other still supplies the same information. Concluding “feature A does not matter” would be misleading.
commonMistakes: Equating feature importance with causal effect.
Comparing raw linear coefficients across differently scaled features.
Ignoring correlated features when interpreting permutation or SHAP values.
followUps: Why can impurity importance be biased?
How would you validate whether an explanation is useful to domain experts?
production: Explanations are useful for debugging, stakeholder review and monitoring unexpected feature dependence. They should be paired with model performance, data checks and domain knowledge rather than used as a safety guarantee.
